WB_Overview: Enables RNA polymerase II-specific DNA-binding transcription factor binding activity; scaffold protein binding activity; and transcription coactivator activity. Involved in several processes, including cell fate commitment involved in formation of primary germ layer; gonad development; and regulation of gene expression. Located in several cellular components, including cell cortex; kinetochore; and pericentriolar material. Expressed in several structures, including ABplpapaap; ABprpapaap; Z1.aa; posterior distal tip cell; and tail hypodermis.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable signaling receptor complex adaptor activity. Involved in several processes, including establishment of mitotic spindle orientation; negative regulation of locomotion; and regulation of egg-laying behavior. Predicted to be located in cytoplasm. Predicted to be part of heterotrimeric G-protein complex. Expressed in several structures, including body wall musculature; germ line; intestine; pharynx; and vulval cell. Used to study cardiovascular system disease. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in several diseases, including Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease dominant intermediate F; artery disease (multiple); and hematologic cancer (multiple). Is an ortholog of human GNB1 (G protein subunit beta 1).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: gpb-1 encodes a heterotrimeric G protein beta subunit that is required during embryonic development for the proper orientation of the mitotic spindle during early cell divisions and thus affects the orientation of early cell division axes, and is also required for larval viability, negatively regulates locomotion and egg-laying, and may affect germline development and osmotic balance; expressed in early embryos with highest expression at cell membranes and colocalizes with asters just before and during early cell divisions (this localization is dependent upon G alpha subunits); adults display high levels of expression in neurons with lower expression in the somatic gonad, vulva, and hypodermal seam cells and expression is also detected in the intestine, pharynx, body wall muscles and in the germline.

Located in several cellular components, including cytoplasmic vesicle; neuronal cell body; and plasma membrane bounded cell projection. Expressed in several structures, including XXX cell; gonad; nerve ring; neurons; and vulva. Used to study Parkinson's disease and diabetes mellitus. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in several diseases, including Alzheimer's disease; glucose metabolism disease (multiple); kidney cancer (multiple); and liver disease (multiple). Is an ortholog of human IGF1R (insulin like growth factor 1 receptor) and INSRR (insulin receptor related receptor).

Narrative: A missense in nos-3 (a Nanos homolog) could disrupt post-transcriptional regulation normally restricted to the germ line but which can influence somatic developmental programs through inter-tissue signaling or regulatory networks, possibly contributing to MCM absence [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=35.9; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="nos-3 required in germ-line development and for regulation of fem-3 mRNA"; WB_Overview="Predicted RNA binding; expressed in germ line"].
rationale: NOS-3 is an RNA-binding protein with roles in germline development and mRNA regulation; although germline-focused, RNA regulation can have broader developmental consequences.

WB_Overview: Enriched in neurons based on RNA-seq studies. Is affected by csr-1 and rrf-2 based on RNA-seq and microarray studies. Is affected by tryptophan; resveratrol; and allantoin based on microarray studies. Is predicted to encode a protein with the following domains: Receptor L-domain superfamily; Receptor L domain; Receptor L-domain; and SPS2 domain-containing protein.
Narrative: A missense in neuron-enriched irld-66 (receptor L-domain protein) could affect cell-surface signaling between AMso and neighboring cells necessary for instructing asymmetric division into MCM neurons, so impaired IRLD-66 function is a plausible contributor [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=39.3; WB_Overview="Enriched in neurons based on RNA-seq; predicted receptor L-domain protein"].
rationale: IRLD-66 is neuron-enriched and encodes receptor L-domain protein; a missense change could affect neuron-glia signaling or extracellular interactions required for AMso division outcome.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable transmembrane transporter activity. Predicted to be involved in chloride transmembrane transport and sulfate transmembrane transport. Predicted to be located in plasma membrane. Expressed in body wall musculature; excretory cell; hypodermis; intestine; and neurons.
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: sulp-1 encodes one of eight C. elegans members of the sulfate permease family of anion transporters; by homology, SULP-1 is predicted to function as an anion transporter that regulates cellular pH and volume via transmembrane movement of electrolytes and fluids; a sulp-1::GFP transcriptional fusion is expressed strongly in several neurons, weakly in hypodermal cells and the intestine, and very faintly in the excretory cell and body wall muscle.
Narrative: A missense in sulp-1, a neuronal sulfate permease, may alter ionic or osmotic environment and signaling in neurons/glia during sexual maturation; such changes can alter cell polarity or signaling that control AMso asymmetric division and MCM production [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=8.9; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="sulp-1 encodes a sulfate permease expressed strongly in several neurons"; WB_Overview="Predicted transmembrane transporter activity"].
rationale: SULP-1 is a sulfate permease expressed in neurons; transporter perturbation can change ionic milieu or signaling that may affect AMso division or differentiation.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable branched-chain-amino-acid transaminase activity. Involved in branched-chain amino acid catabolic process; embryo development; and nematode larval development. Acts upstream of or within determination of adult lifespan. Located in mitochondrion. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in hypervalinemia and hyperleucine-isoleucinemia. Is an ortholog of human BCAT1 (branched chain amino acid transaminase 1) and BCAT2 (branched chain amino acid transaminase 2).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: bcat-1 encodes a branched-chain amino acid aminotransferase that, by homology, is predicted to catalyze the first reaction in the catabolism of essential branched-chain amino acids such as leucine, isoleucine, and valine; in C. elegans, large-scale RNA-mediated interference (RNAi) screens indicate that bcat-1 activity is required for embryonic and larval development.

There is no evidence in the summary that bcat-1 or mitochondrial hyperactivity alters the AMso asymmetric division program or instructs neuronal vs glial fate decisions required to explain loss of MCM neurons. ; PMID33589689: Irrelevant - score:1 Reason:The paper describes behavioral effects of neuronal bcat-1 knockdown and a drug-screening platform for Parkinson-like movement defects, but contains no data or mechanistic discussion of asymmetric division, AMso-to-MCM specification, or glial-to-neuronal fate transitions. BCAT-1 is presented as a metabolic enzyme affecting neuronal function/behavior rather than a regulator of cell fate or asymmetric division in the male-specific MCM lineage.
Narrative: A missense in bcat-1 may affect branched-chain amino acid metabolism essential for growth and developmental timing; altered metabolic state can shift timing/competence of AMso division during sexual maturation leading to missing MCM neurons [Effect=missense_variant; impact_bucket=MODERATE; QUAL=10.0; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="bcat-1 required for embryonic and larval development"; WB_Overview="Mitochondrial enzyme involved in BCAA catabolism"].
rationale: BCAT-1 is required for larval development and amino-acid metabolism; metabolic perturbations can influence developmental timing and competence of AMso divisions.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase activity. Predicted to be involved in protein N-linked glycosylation. Predicted to be located in endoplasmic reticulum membrane. Human ortholog(s) of this gene implicated in congenital disorder of glycosylation Il. Is an ortholog of human ALG9 (ALG9 alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase).
Narrative: Although synonymous, the algn-9 variant may tag cis-regulatory change or splicing alteration in an N-linked glycosylation enzyme; defective glycosylation can impair cell-surface receptors or adhesion molecules that direct AMso asymmetric division and MCM specification [Effect=synonymous_variant; impact_bucket=LOW; QUAL=38.8; WB_Overview="Predicted alpha-1,2-mannosyltransferase activity; involved in protein N-linked glycosylation"].
rationale: ALGN-9 is involved in N-linked glycosylation; glycoprotein processing defects can perturb cell-surface signaling important for asymmetric divisions.

WB_Overview: Predicted to enable DNA-binding transcription factor activity, RNA polymerase II-specific and RNA polymerase II cis-regulatory region sequence-specific DNA binding activity. Predicted to be involved in brain development; neuron differentiation; and regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II. Predicted to be located in nucleus. Expressed widely. Is an ortholog of human NOTO (notochord homeobox).
MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB: ceh-100 is a divergent homeobox gene; it encodes 12 homeodomains; it is located close to ceh-99 on chromosome II and may be a paralog; most homeodomain proteins bind DNA and function as transcription factors; ceh-100 is involved in embryo development and response to food; ceh-100 is expressed widely.
Narrative: An upstream variant in the homeobox gene ceh-100 could alter transcription factor levels during development; changes in a transcriptional regulator can perturb gene-expression programs required for AMso to produce MCM neurons [Effect=upstream_gene_variant; impact_bucket=MODIFIER; QUAL=23.7; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="ceh-100 encodes a divergent homeobox gene with roles in embryo development and widespread expression"; WB_Overview="Predicted DNA-binding transcription factor activity"].
rationale: CEH-100 is a divergent homeobox (transcription factor) gene; upstream variation could alter transcription programs that influence neuronal fate specification.

WB_Overview: Enriched in head mesodermal cell; muscle cell; and neurons based on RNA-seq and microarray studies. Is affected by several genes including cyc-1; etr-1; and pry-1 based on microarray and RNA-seq studies. Is affected by thirteen chemicals including Psoralens; allantoin; and Sirolimus based on RNA-seq and microarray studies. Is predicted to encode a protein with the following domains: Leucine-rich repeat, cysteine-containing subtype and Leucine-rich repeat domain superfamily. Is an ortholog of human FBXL7 (F-box and leucine rich repeat protein 7).
Narrative: An intronic variant in ark-1 could influence expression of a kinase that negatively regulates EGF receptor signaling and enforces binary fate decisions; perturbation may disrupt lateral fate enforcement during AMso lineage decisions, allowing glial fate to predominate over MCM neuron fate [Effect=intron_variant; impact_bucket=MODIFIER; QUAL=17.2; distilled_mechanism="ARK-1 is induced by LIN-12/Notch and acts as a tyrosine kinase that negatively regulates EGF-receptor/MAPK signaling to enforce lateral binary cell-fate decisions"; MANUAL_DESCRIPTION_WB="ark-1 inhibits LET-23/EGFR signaling"].
rationale: ARK-1 is a tyrosine kinase that enforces lateral binary fate decisions (antagonizes EGF signaling), so perturbation could subtly change binary cell-fate choices tied to glia vs neuron outcomes.
